changes: Account-row locks serialize issuance, failed guesses, one-time claims, credential changes, MFA proof issuance/completion, and password-login session creation.
SQL increments bound failed guesses at five and burn the code on the fifth failure; code matches cannot bypass the cap.
Code claim checks live wall-clock expiration and consumes atomically; invalid password types, too-short strings, and bcrypt-truncated inputs over 72 bytes fail before consuming a valid code.
Local reset changes password, resets lockout, burns all pending reset/MFA proofs and revokes sessions in the same transaction. Local write failure rolls everything back.

Provider reset/change first durably stores an unusable pending credential revision, consumes reset/MFA proofs and revokes sessions. Only then does it call Supabase once under account lock. Confirmed completion stores a fresh unusable revision; failure leaves pending recovery state and exposed 503 requiring a new reset code.

MFA proof context includes hashed credential revision. Stale password verification cannot issue a proof/session after reset or credential changes; inline backup consumption and session insertion are now in the same transaction.

Email/phone confirmation atomically consumes its code and sets the verified flag under the fresh account lock. Combined confirmation uses the same bounded helpers. Phone changes via verification send invalidate outstanding phone codes.
Failed delivery burns only the specifically issued code; logs no longer include contact details or raw provider delivery errors.

verification.isolation: Each test file creates and cleans an isolated PostgreSQL schema on loopback-only approved test database. Provider mutation is faked at fetch boundary; no remote provider calls or production records.
verification.expected_errors: Synthetic database failures and intentionally exposed recovery 503 errors appear in the successful test output.

contracts_and_impact: No schema, migration, dependency, CI, security-folder, commit, deployment or production changes.
Preserved successful auth response shapes and Supabase UID-based authentication; unique placeholder suffix remains unusable for bcrypt fallback.
Password input now explicitly rejects non-strings and UTF-8 input above 72 bytes to prevent bcrypt truncation; frontend/API callers must respect the limit.
Existing outstanding MFA proofs without credentialHash are invalidated and require fresh password login.
Local authenticated change preserves existing sessions but consumes pending reset/MFA authorizations; provider changes revoke sessions because uncertain external status requires recovery.
Phone-profile changes must use the same account lock and invalidate phone_verify codes; root owns that paired route update.
Shared verification response fields remain unchanged; older superseded code rows are rejected in favor of the newest purpose-specific code.
risks_and_unverified: Independent review and full integrated suite remain parent-owned; focused success is not production readiness or a security guarantee.
Provider timeout and successful-provider/failed-local-finalization tested with fake Supabase boundary. No live Supabase staging test, production call or literal process termination performed.

A provider call that times out may still apply remotely after local cancellation; PostgreSQL cannot guarantee cross-system atomicity or external ordering. Pending state and new-code recovery expose uncertainty; operational investigation may be required.
Provider update holds a database account lock/connection for existing bounded provider HTTP timeout; failures require email/SMS delivery to recover.
Existing forgot-password delivery remains asynchronous and returns a neutral account-enumeration-resistant response; actual email/SMS delivery has not been validated in this increment.
Sensitive auth changes require qualified human review before production release.
learn: Parent is creating one Edirae Learn breakdown and INDEX entry for the complete logical audit/fix task; no separate increment breakdown written.
